title: Classic Traveller character record
description:
What ctchargen writes, as this build writes it. A description of the output, kept honest by CI - not a promise to records already written. Across builds nothing is promised: changing the procedure, the dice-stream consumption order, or an event's wording changes the output for a given seed, and that is an ordinary change. What makes that affordable is that a record is regenerable from its seed and its inputs, and nothing in it is hand-written.

Two of the optional benefit fields cannot appear together in any character this tool can generate. Book 1 p. 9 prints Travellers' Aid only in the Navy and Marines columns of Mustering Out Table 1, and the two starships only in the Scout and Merchant columns, and a character serves one service. So no valid record carries both travellersAid and ships. That is a fact about the rules rather than a gap in the fixtures, which is why character.complete.json shows the ships and not the membership.

name.description: Blank unless --name supplied one. Book 1 pp. 4-5 give naming as advice, not a table, so nothing generates one.

upp.description: The Universal Personality Profile (p. 8): the six characteristics as hexadecimal digits in rolled order. Derived from characteristics, and stored beside them so a reader need not re-derive it.

characteristics.description: The six of p. 4, numeric. A value may reach 0 only through aging (E010); everything else floors at 1, and nothing exceeds 15.

age.description: Whole years, plus the months only a medical crisis recovery adds (pp. 7-8). Books 1-3 have no calendar and no birthdate rules, so the record carries an age and a count of terms, not a date.

terms.description: Terms of service, four years each (p. 5). Zero for a civilian. No upper bound: a 12 on the reenlistment throw recurs (E003).

how.description: P. 5. Declining is a complete record: an eighteen-year-old civilian (E001).

rank.description: An index into the service's own Table of Ranks (p. 10). Absent where the character holds none: rank 0 is not commissioned, and the Scouts and Other print no ranks at all.

rankTitle.description: What the Table of Ranks calls that rank in that service (p. 10).

skills.description: Name and level, sorted by name. Where the rules demand a specific weapon, the name is that weapon's: p. 25's own list records Dagger-1, not Blade Combat.

travellersAid.description: Membership, achievable only once per character; a duplicate roll is wasted (p. 22).

weapons.description: Weapons received as benefits, which is narrower than the weapons held: expertise may be taken only in one received as a benefit (p. 22).

tons.description: The hull each is built on: Book 2 p. 18 for the Type S, p. 19 for the Type A.

paymentYears.description: Years of payments left on a Free Trader (pp. 22-23). A scout ship is held without title and carries none.

scoutShipsLost.description: Scout ships a duplicate roll lost. P. 23: "Only one scout ship may be acquired by a character, and throws resulting in additional ships are lost."

annualRetirementPay.description: P. 21. Earned by leaving at the end of the fifth term or later, whatever caused it, and not available to the Scouts or Other.

departure.description: How the service ended. Absent for a civilian, who never joined one.

characteristic.description: The characteristic that reached zero, on a death by medical crisis (pp. 7-8, E008).

title.description: Assessed once, at the end of generation, against the final Social Standing, for every character including the dead - who are assessed but not asked (E011).

rank.description: Book 3 p. 22, for Social Standing 11 through 15.

inputs.description: Everything the generation was given, so that a record says what made it.

seed.description: The one recorded seed, filling both words of the PCG state. A seed the tool draws for itself is bounded to 2^53-1, above which a reader parsing JSON numbers as doubles would round it silently; an explicit --seed is the operator's own number and is written as given.

service.description: Present when --service forced the enlistment attempt. It forces the attempt only: the throw is still made, and a failed throw still goes to the draft.

errata.description: Every recorded reading of docs/ERRATA.md that governed this record, in id order. A reading applied without appearing here is the one defect no gate catches.

build.description: The build that wrote the record, from debug.ReadBuildInfo. With cross-build reproduction unpromised, naming the build is the whole of what makes a record reasonable about.

events.description: The generation record: every step entered, throw made, choice answered and consequence, with monotonic sequence numbers. Walk it against Book 1 to audit any character.

service.description: The six of the Prior Service Table (p. 10), spelled as p. 5 lists them (E012).

dice.description: The dice as rolled, first die then second. The record logs the dice and not only their total, because that is what an auditor walks against the page.

target.description: The throw's target in the book's own notation (pp. 2-3). Absent on a one-die roll, which has no target to meet.

point.description: One per method of the Decider interface, which is what closes the set. docs/POLICY.md carries one row per method.

because.description: The throw or choice that caused this. Absent where the consequence follows from the procedure itself.
